newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.87/88 after sharp fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.87/88 after sharp fall.

text.p: The rupee closed at 35.8775/8825 against the dollar on Monday after touching an early low of 35.99, dealers said.
The rupee opened the day at 35.91/93 compared to the previous close of 35.89/90, but fell sharply in early inter-bank trade largely on political uncertainties, they said.
The rupee fell to a low of 35.99 on Monday. A state-run bank dealer said there were some deals even at 36 rupees, but other dealers said they could not confirm this.
Many dealers expected importers to rush for dollar cover after Congress Party's Sunday statement that it was withdrawing its support to the ruling United Front government.
Some dealers said the sharp fall stemmed partly from speculative bidding but others said it was because many banks had sold dollars over the past week and were caught short.
"Inter-bank speculation can't decide the day," said a dealer at a state-run bank. He said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) made enquiries with banks.
"This acted as a dampener and normal (dollar) supplies resumed," said the dealer.
The rest of the day saw the rupee move in one way - up.
"Supplies came from all sources -- from exporters, merchants, from position cutting and year-end adjustments."

The chief of international division at a state-run bank said the rupee's fall early in the day was the market's reflection of a steep fall in the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share benchmark index on Monday.
Dealers said the forward dollar market lacked direction on Monday.
The six month annualised premium closed at 6.74 percent compared to the previous close of 6.69 percent, dealers said.
"At the end of the day, it was like any other day except that RBI didn't buy dollars today," said a dealer.
The foreign exchange market will be inactive on Tuesday as banks across India are closed for customer transactions to finalise the accounts for the year ending March 31, 1997.
